blocks.task_summary: Find vectors AB = (−3,−2,0) and AC = (−2,1,−7), then find the Cartesian equation of plane Π1 through A, B, C in the form ax+by+cz=d.
accepted_alternatives: Parametric plane form r = A + s·AB + t·AC, express x,y,z in terms of s,t, eliminate parameters to obtain 2x−3y−z=6

evidence.basis: (a)(i) attempts to find either AB or AC (M1); AB=(−3,−2,0) and AC=(−2,1,−7) A1. (a)(ii) METHOD 1: attempts to find AB×AC (M1); AB×AC=(14,−21,−7) A1; EITHER equation form 2x−3y−z=d (A1), substitutes a valid point M1, d=6 A1; OR uses r·n=a·n (M1, A1). METHOD 2: parametric form A1, forms equations M1, eliminates parameters M1, obtains 2x−3y−z=6 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Verify that the vector equation of line L (intersection of Π1 and Π2) can be written as r = (0,−2,0) + λ(1,1,−1).
method_path: substitute x=λ, y=−2+λ, z=−λ into Π1: 2λ−3(−2+λ)−(−λ)=6 → 6=6
both equations hold identically for all λ
accepted_alternatives: Cross product of normals (2,−3,−1)×(3,−1,2)=(−7,−7,7) parallel to (1,1,−1); verify B(0,−2,0) lies in both planes.
Solve 2x−3y−z=6 and 3x−y+2z=2 simultaneously to obtain parametric form x=λ, y=−2+λ, z=−λ.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: substitutes r=(0,−2,0)+λ(1,1,−1) into Π1 and Π2 (M1); Π1: 2λ−3(−2+λ)−(−λ)=6 and Π2: 3λ−(−2+λ)+2(−λ)=2 A1. METHOD 2: attempts cross product of normals (M1); (2,−3,−1)×(3,−1,2)=(−7,−7,7) OR dot product verifications (M1); substitutes (0,−2,0) into both planes A1. METHOD 3: attempts to solve 2x−3y−z=6 and 3x−y+2z=2 (M1); obtains x=λ, y=−2−λ, z=λ? [2 marks].

blocks.task_summary: Show that at the intersection P of L and plane Π3: 2x−2z=3, λ=3/4, and hence find the coordinates of P.

evidence.basis: (c)(i) substitutes the equation of L into the equation of Π3 (M1); 2λ+2λ=3⇒λ=3/4 A1 AG. (ii) P has coordinates (3/4,−5/4,−3/4) A1. [3 marks].

blocks.task_summary: Find the reflection B′ of B(0,−2,0) in plane Π3: 2x−2z=3, then find the vector equation of the line formed when L is reflected in Π3.
method_path: construct line through B normal to Π3: r = (0,−2,0) + μ(2,0,−2)
direction of reflected line: B′ − P = (3/4,−3/4,−3/4)
reflected line: r = (3/2,−2,−3/2) + λ(3/4,−3/4,−3/4) or equivalent
accepted_alternatives: Use dot-product condition to find μ on normal line.
Use plane parallel to Π3 through B′ and solve simultaneously with L.
Find direction via vector reflection formula using normal.

evidence.basis: (d)(i) normal to Π3 is (2,0,−2) (A1); considers line normal to Π3 passing through B(0,−2,0) (M1); r=(0,−2,0)+μ(2,0,−2) A1; EITHER finds intersection with Π3 (M1), 4μ+4μ=3, μ=3/8 A1, point (3/4,−2,−3/4); THEN another point on reflected line r=(0,−2,0)+(3/4)(2,0,−2) (A1); B′=(3/2,−2,−3/2) A1.
(d)(ii) EITHER attempts direction using P and B′ (M1): PB′=(3/4,−3/4,−3/4); OR vector approach PB′=PB+BB′ (M1); THEN r=(3/2,−2,−3/2)+λ(3/4,−3/4,−3/4) or equivalent A1. [9 marks].
